key_insight: The paper shows that a backward-mapping, genome-guided pipeline can translate device targets into chemically interpretable rules to discover phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: This provides an interpretable inverse-design workflow for accelerating materials screening toward safer, stable optoelectronic semiconductors.
method: Filtered 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions with halide-aware formability rules
Encoded materials using six chemical-genome descriptor families and trained evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates
Applied SHAP interpretation and DFT phenotype closure to validate top candidates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a funnel from 13,088 candidates to seven DFT-validated double perovskites with stability, band-gap, optical, dielectric, and transport properties checked.
watch_item: The approach depends on surrogate accuracy and PBE-based screening, so experimental synthesis and higher-level electronic-structure validation are still needed.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
